title.narrative: Provision of emergency WASH assistance to IDPs and host communities in North Darfur.

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan hosts the world's largest population of internally displaced persons, with over 6.5 million displaced internally and an additional 2 million seeking refuge in neighboring countries. The inability to move to safer areas is a major challenge for those trapped in high-conflict zones like Zamzam camp in El Fasher, worsened by the high cost of travel. While conflict has slightly decreased in some western areas, North Darfur has experienced an escalation. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough this proposed project, Solidarites International (SI) will participate in addressing, in synergy with other actors such as Relief International (RI), the food crisis in El Fasher, an area categorized as IPC System 4. SI will work on improving hygiene practices and providing emergency water and sanitation services for conflict-affected populations in El Fasher locality, thus addressing urgent needs for basic water, sanitation, and hygiene services in response to increased demands due to conflict and related internal displacement. SI’s emergency WASH assistance will be done in synergy with other actors who plan to intervene in El Fasher, notably through CBPF funding such as RI. The latter will for example focus on food security and livelihood support as well as improving access to health and nutrition services: SI’s emergency WASH activities will come in complementarity to these activities allowing access to hygiene materials, clean water and sanitation which will contribute to reduce the prevalence of water-borne diseases and diseases – including those related to crops’ soil contamination – that could aggravate individuals’ already critical food security situation. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSI aims to integrate conflict sensitivity into all its activities, involving comprehensive conflict analysis, adapting activities to the context, and adhering to the "do no harm" principle. This includes community engagement, transparent beneficiary selection, and risk assessment. Collaboration, monitoring and evaluation, staff training, feedback mechanisms, and flexible programming are key. The goal is to ensure activities do not escalate conflicts, but instead promote peace, stability, and provide timely assistance to vulnerable communities in conflict zones.ltbrgtlt/pgt
